priorStories.headline: Judge halts FCC’s early ABC license reviews
priorStories.body:
A federal judge blocked the Federal Communications Commission from continuing early license-renewal proceedings against eight ABC-owned television stations while litigation proceeds.

U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan found ABC likely to succeed on its claim that the proceedings retaliated against protected speech. The preliminary injunction pauses the reviews; it is not a final ruling on that claim. The court also denied the government’s motion to dismiss the lawsuit.

The FCC disputed the decision and said it expected to prevail.

sources.name: US District Court for the District of Columbia via The Desk

priorStories.headline: US inflation gauge records 3.8% annual rise
priorStories.body:
Consumer prices measured by the personal consumption expenditures index rose 3.8% in the year through October and 0.3% from September, the Bureau of Economic Analysis reported November 25. Excluding food and energy, prices increased 3.3% annually and 0.3% for the month.

Personal income rose 0.7% in October. Consumer spending increased 0.3% before accounting for inflation, but was essentially unchanged after adjusting for higher prices. The personal saving rate was 4.1%.
